title: Queued request starvation during burst peaks — dedup+replenish patch
creator: Maya Singh
description: Customer-reported recurring capacity shortfalls during sustained traffic spikes in Dedicated pools. Symptoms: long tail of queued requests (>10s) for small tenants even though pool reports headroom; burst credits did not replenish for minutes and requests were starved by the allocation queue. Affects reserved pools with cross-zone replica sets when an eviction or node transition occurs. Root cause hypothesis: race between leader-driven burst ledger reconciliation and local allocator dedup path that marked slots as occupied while the global ledger had not refreshed, combined with delayed cross-zone eviction signal. This ticket tracks investigation, patch, rollout, customer comms, and postmortem.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated reserved pool with multi-AZ nodes and two small tenants. 2) Drive a sustained burst load to tenant A just below its burst limit. 3) Trigger a simulated eviction in one AZ (drain a node) to cause leader handover. 4) Generate concurrent short requests from tenant B. 5) Observe allocation queue depths and burst ledger age. Expected: brief reconciling gap but no multi-minute starvation. Observed: queued requests for tenant B back up and have high latency while dashboard shows nominal available tokens.
root_cause: A combination of (a) burst ledger reconciliation only on leader election + periodic polling (default 30s), (b) allocator dedup mechanism that preemptively reserved slots based on stale local state, and (c) cross-zone eviction events delaying token replenishment. When leadership moved, allocator continued relying on stale local cache and treat candidate slots as occupied, while the global ledger did not yet credit burst tokens — resulting in visible headroom mismatch and queued requests.
fix_summary: 1) Add immediate ledger refresh in scale-controller on leadership change and on eviction events. 2) Tighten allocator dedup window: ensure reservations created from local cache include a short TTL and require confirmation from the reconciled ledger before long-held reservations. 3) Add exponential backoff + jitter to cross-zone eviction handshake to prevent cascade. 4) Add unit and integration tests simulating leader flip + eviction + concurrent requests. 5) Backport hotfix to runtime-1.24 and dedicated-controller-2026.02 releases.
rollback_plan: If the patch causes regression in allocation fairness, revert scale-controller PR and enable a temporary knob that forces pre-patch ledger polling (poll-interval=5s) while we iterate. Revert path validated in staging.
rollout_plan: Canary to low-traffic US-West region: enable patched scale-controller in 10% of reserved pools -> monitor queue depth and headroom mismatch metrics for 2 hours -> expand to 50% -> full. Apply allocator patch behind feature flag gated by operator. Coordinate with SRE for K8s node drain window adjustment.
communication: Initial customer e-mail sent 2026-03-03 to AcmeRetail describing mitigation and plan. Status updates sent 2026-03-06 and 2026-03-12. Post-fix apology + detailed timeline will be delivered after verification.
